summary: Both prior required revisions are resolved. The spacing and notation pass preserves the inspected proof text and identifiers, and the maximum-neighbourhood definition now supports the intended graph-degree reading. Sampled source-map entries distinguish imported classifications from new reductions. Added historical attribution agrees with the accessible primary preprint. No new copyeditor revision is required at this phase; whole-proof acceptance and comprehensive text-reuse clearance are not asserted.

revisions.result: Resolved: Sections 4–6 match exactly under that normalization; their 402 ordered digit runs and arithmetic/comparison-sign sequence agree. Both pinned-commit occurrences, all four archive-version identifiers and Lean 4.26.0 remain intact. The requested examples have normal spacing.

revisions.action: Read the new N[max] and N43 definitions and checked every later neighbourhood inequality against the cap15 and degree16 assembly meanings.
revisions.result: Resolved: N[max] ≤ c explicitly quantifies over every actual member, so N[max] ≤ 43 at size 68 yields graph minimum degree at least 25 without confusing the maximum with μ.

checks.scope: Maximum-neighbourhood notation and its later use
checks.method: Inspected Section 3 definitions and all scalar neighbourhood inequalities in Sections 5.1 and 6, comparing with the previously inspected cap15 and degree16 assemblies.
checks.observation: N[R] is a set, μ is the minimum cardinality, and N[max] is the maximum cardinality. The universal upper-bound meaning and actual N43 anchor are explicit. The graph-degree formula |F| − |N[R]| makes the later minimum-degree conclusion readable with its correct quantifier.
